```{r}
# Function to process each dataset
process_dataset <- function(data_path, sample_name) {
  # Read the data
  data <- read.csv(data_path)
  
  # Remove the first column (assumed to be an index)
  data <- data[, -1]
  
  # Rename "annotation" column to "CyTOF_annotation"
  colnames(data)[colnames(data) == "annotation"] <- "CyTOF_annotation"
  
  # Set cell IDs
  cell_ids <- paste0(sample_name, "_cell", seq_len(nrow(data)))
  rownames(data) <- cell_ids
  
  # Identify metadata columns
  metadata_cols <- c("CyTOF_annotation", "tsne1", "tsne2")
  
  # Adjust indices based on sample if needed
  if (sample_name == "Human_AT_Stanford") {
    cytof_indices <- 2:40
  } else {
    cytof_indices <- 1:40
  }
  qbc_indices <- 41:174
  
  # Add modality suffixes to marker columns
  colnames(data)[cytof_indices] <- paste0(colnames(data)[cytof_indices], "_CyTOF")
  colnames(data)[qbc_indices] <- paste0(colnames(data)[qbc_indices], "_QBC")
  
  # Update marker columns after renaming
  marker_cols <- setdiff(colnames(data), metadata_cols)
  
  # Extract counts matrix (only marker columns)
  counts <- data[, marker_cols]
  
  # Extract metadata
  metadata <- data[, metadata_cols]
  
  # Transpose the counts matrix to features x cells
  counts_t <- t(counts)
  
  # Ensure cell IDs are set correctly
  colnames(counts_t) <- cell_ids
  
  # Convert counts_t to a numeric matrix
  counts_t <- as.matrix(counts_t)
  mode(counts_t) <- "numeric"
  
  # Create Seurat object with counts_t as counts in 'Protein' assay
  seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts_t, assay = "Protein", meta.data = metadata, project = sample_name)
  
  # Set default assay to 'Protein'
  DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "Protein"
  
  # Add sample name as metadata
  seurat_obj$sample <- sample_name
  
  return(seurat_obj)
}
```

```{r}
# Normalize and identify variable features for each Human Seurat object using CLR normalization
human_seurat_list <- lapply(human_seurat_list, function(seurat_obj) {
  DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "Protein"
  seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 1, assay = "Protein")
  seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000, assay = "Protein")
  return(seurat_obj)
})
```

```{r}
  seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000, assay = "Protein")

})
```

#Rename marker names by replacing instances of .1-QBC with .QBC in your human_integrated and rhesus_integrated Seurat objects
```{r}
#Renaming Function
rename_markers <- function(seurat_obj) {
  # Step 1: Access the 'integrated' assay
  integrated_assay <- seurat_obj[["integrated"]]
  
  # Ensure the 'integrated' assay exists
  if (is.null(integrated_assay)) {
    stop("The 'integrated' assay does not exist in the Seurat object.")
  }
  
  # Step 2: Get current feature names from the 'data' slot
  data_mat <- integrated_assay@data
  current_markers <- rownames(data_mat)
  length_current_markers <- length(current_markers)
  cat("Number of current markers:", length_current_markers, "\n")
  
  # Ensure that current_markers is not NULL or empty
  if (is.null(current_markers) || length_current_markers == 0) {
    stop("No feature names found in the 'data' slot of the 'integrated' assay.")
  }
  
  # Step 3: Replace '.1-QBC' with '.QBC' only if at the end
  new_markers <- sub("\\.1-QBC$", ".QBC", current_markers)
  
  # Step 4: Remove numeric suffixes greater than 1 before '-QBC'
  new_markers_unique <- sub("\\.[2-9][0-9]*-QBC$", "-QBC", new_markers)
  length_new_markers_unique <- length(new_markers_unique)
  cat("Number of new unique markers:", length_new_markers_unique, "\n")
  
  # Step 5: Check for duplicates
  if (any(duplicated(new_markers_unique))) {
    dup_markers <- unique(new_markers_unique[duplicated(new_markers_unique)])
    cat("Duplicate markers after renaming:", paste(dup_markers, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    stop("Renaming resulted in duplicate feature names. Please ensure all feature names are unique.")
  }
  
  # Step 6: Ensure lengths match
  if (length_current_markers != length_new_markers_unique) {
    stop("Mismatch in the number of markers before and after renaming.")
  }
  
  # Step 7: Update feature names in 'data' slot
  rownames(data_mat) <- new_markers_unique
  integrated_assay@data <- data_mat
  
  # Step 8: Update feature names in 'scale.data' slot if it exists
  if (!is.null(integrated_assay@scale.data) && nrow(integrated_assay@scale.data) > 0) {
    scale_mat <- integrated_assay@scale.data
    scale_features <- rownames(scale_mat)
    n_rows_scale_mat <- nrow(scale_mat)
    cat("Number of rows in scale.data:", n_rows_scale_mat, "\n")
    
    # Map old feature names to new names
    new_scale_features <- new_markers_unique[match(scale_features, current_markers)]
    
    # Check for NA values
    if (any(is.na(new_scale_features))) {
      missing_features <- scale_features[is.na(new_scale_features)]
      cat("Features in scale.data not found in current markers:", paste(missing_features, collapse = ", "), "\n")
      stop("Some features in 'scale.data' could not be matched to new marker names.")
    }
    
    # Assign new feature names to scale.data
    rownames(scale_mat) <- new_scale_features
    integrated_assay@scale.data <- scale_mat
  }
  
  # Step 9: Update feature names in 'meta.features' if it exists
  if (!is.null(integrated_assay@meta.features)) {
    if (nrow(integrated_assay@meta.features) != length(new_markers_unique)) {
      stop("Number of new markers does not match number of rows in 'meta.features'.")
    }
    rownames(integrated_assay@meta.features) <- new_markers_unique
  }
  
  # Step 10: Update the variable features in the assay
  if (length(integrated_assay@var.features) > 0) {
    var_features <- integrated_assay@var.features
    
    # Map old variable features to new names
    var_features_new <- new_markers_unique[match(var_features, current_markers)]
    
    # Check for NAs in var_features_new
    if (any(is.na(var_features_new))) {
      missing_var_features <- var_features[is.na(var_features_new)]
      cat("Variable features not found in current markers:", paste(missing_var_features, collapse = ", "), "\n")
      # Remove NA entries
      var_features_new <- var_features_new[!is.na(var_features_new)]
    }
    
    integrated_assay@var.features <- var_features_new
  }
  
  # Step 11: Assign the modified assay back to the Seurat object
  seurat_obj[["integrated"]] <- integrated_assay
  
  # Step 12: Return the updated Seurat object
  return(seurat_obj)
}
```

#Scale the Data


```{r}
# Scale rhesus_integrated dataset using cross-species markers derived QBC readings

```

#PCA
```{r}
# Run PCA on human_integrated using ONLY cross-species markers derived QBC readings
human_integrated <- RunPCA(human_integrated, features = cross_species_markers_qbc_panel)

#The elbow plot helps visualize the amount of variation captured by each PC
#A visualization that is useful for determining how many PCs to include
#Look for the point where the explained variance starts to level off (“the elbow”) to decide how many PCs to use
file_path <- file.path(output_path, "human_elbowplot.pdf")
pdf(file_path)
ElbowPlot(human_integrated)
dev.off()
```

#Perform Clustering
```{r}
#FindNeighbors() constructs a KNN graph based on the PCs
human_integrated <- FindNeighbors(human_integrated, dims = 1:7)

#computing the neighborhood graph and find clusters
#FindClusters() identifies clusters using the Louvain algorithm
#The resolution parameter affects the number of clusters; higher values lead to more clusters
human_integrated <- FindClusters(human_integrated, resolution = 0.5)
```

```{r}
#FindNeighbors() constructs a KNN graph based on the PCs
rhesus_integrated <- FindNeighbors(rhesus_integrated, dims = 1:8)

#computing the neighborhood graph and find clusters
#FindClusters() identifies clusters using the Louvain algorithm
#The resolution parameter affects the number of clusters; higher values lead to more clusters
rhesus_integrated <- FindClusters(rhesus_integrated, resolution = 0.5)
```

#Analyze Cluster Markers for Cluster Annotation
```{r}
# Find markers for each cluster - human

human_integrated.markers <- FindAllMarkers(human_integrated, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.25)

human_integrated.markers %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    slice_max(n = 20, order_by = avg_log2FC)

file_path_csv <- file.path(output_path, "human_integrated_top_20_markers_for_every_cluster.csv")

write.csv(human_integrated.markers, file = file_path_csv, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
    slice_max(n = 20, order_by = avg_log2FC)
```

#Species Difference Analysis of CyTOF cell surface and phospho signaling using "QBC_annotation_cross_species"
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Define Marker Lists
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Purpose: Specify the CyTOF surface markers and phospho-protein markers for plotting.
# The names are adjusted to match the feature names in your Seurat objects.

# --- Surface Markers ---
surface_marker_map <- data.frame(
  human = c("CD235a-CyTOF", "CD45-CyTOF", "CD61-CyTOF", "CD7-CyTOF", "CD33-CyTOF", "CD11c-CyTOF",
            "CD123-CyTOF", "CD14-CyTOF", "CD11b-CyTOF", "CD8a-CyTOF", "CD4-CyTOF", "CD3-CyTOF",
            "CD66b-CyTOF", "CD16-CyTOF", "CD1c-CyTOF", "CD141-CyTOF", "CD45RA-CyTOF",
            "CD161-CyTOF", "CCR7-CyTOF", "CD19-CyTOF", "IgM-CyTOF", "CD56-CyTOF", "HLA-DR-CyTOF"),
  rhesus = c("CD235a-CyTOF", "CD45-CyTOF", "CD61-CyTOF", "CD7-CyTOF", "CD33-CyTOF", "CD11c-CyTOF",
             "CD123-CyTOF", "CD14-CyTOF", "CD11b-CyTOF", "CD8a-CyTOF", "CD4-CyTOF", "CD3-CyTOF",
             "CD66b-CyTOF", "CD16-CyTOF", "CD1c-CyTOF", "CD141-CyTOF", "CD45RA-CyTOF",
             "CD161-CyTOF", "CCR7-CyTOF", "CD20-CyTOF", "IgM-CyTOF", "CD56-CyTOF", "HLA-DR-CyTOF"),
  display_name = c("CD235a", "CD45", "CD61", "CD7", "CD33", "CD11c",
                   "CD123", "CD14", "CD11b", "CD8a", "CD4", "CD3",
                   "CD66b", "CD16", "CD1c", "CD141", "CD45RA",
                   "CD161", "CCR7", "CD19/20", "IgM", "CD56", "HLA-DR")
)


# --- Phospho-protein Markers ---
phospho_markers_features <- c(
  "pSTAT1.Y701.-CyTOF", "pSTAT3.Y705.-CyTOF", "pSTAT4.Y693.-CyTOF", "pSTAT5.Y694.-CyTOF", "pSTAT6.Y691.-CyTOF",
  "pCREB.S133.-CyTOF", "pMAPKAPK2.T334.-CyTOF", "pS6.S235.S236.-CyTOF", "pZAP70.Syk.Y319.Y352.-CyTOF",
  "pERK1.2.T202.Y204.-CyTOF", "pP38.MAPK.T180.Y182.-CyTOF", "pPLCg2.Y579.-CyTOF",
  "pTBK1.NAK.S172.-CyTOF", "p4EBP1.T37.T46.-CyTOF", "IkBa.amino.terminal-CyTOF"
)

# --- NEW: Robust function to create clean display names ---
# This function replaces the faulty gsub chain.
clean_phospho_names <- function(feature_names) {
  sapply(feature_names, function(name) {
    # Handle the special case of IkBa first
    if (grepl("IkBa.amino.terminal-CyTOF", name)) {
      return("IkBa")
    }
    
    # Clean the name using regex capture groups for precision
    name <- sub("(.*)\\.(.*)\\.-CyTOF", "\\1(\\2)", name)
    
    # Further refine names with slashes for clarity
    name <- gsub("pZAP70.Syk", "pZAP70/Syk", name, fixed = TRUE)
    name <- gsub("pTBK1.NAK", "pTBK1/NAK", name, fixed = TRUE)
    name <- gsub("pS6.S235.S236", "pS6(S235/S236)", name, fixed = TRUE)
    name <- gsub("p4EBP1.T37.T46", "p4EBP1(T37/T46)", name, fixed = TRUE)
    name <- gsub("pERK1.2", "pERK1/2", name, fixed = TRUE)
    name <- gsub("pP38.MAPK", "pP38", name, fixed = TRUE)
    
    return(name)
  }, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}


# Apply the new function to get clean names
phospho_display_names <- clean_phospho_names(phospho_markers_features)

# Create the final mapping data frame for phospho markers
phospho_marker_map <- data.frame(
    feature_name = phospho_markers_features,
    display_name = phospho_display_names
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate Average Expression
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Purpose: Calculate the mean expression for each marker across the
#          'QBC_annotation_cross_species' clusters.

# Set the identity to our target clusters
Idents(human_integrated_annotated) <- "QBC_annotation_cross_species"
Idents(rhesus_integrated_annotated) <- "QBC_annotation_cross_species"

# Function to safely calculate average expression
get_avg_expression <- function(seurat_obj, features) {
  # Find which of the requested features are actually in the object
  features_present <- features[features %in% rownames(seurat_obj)]
  if (length(features_present) == 0) {
    warning("None of the specified features were found in the Seurat object.")
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Calculate average expression using the 'integrated' assay data
  avg_expr <- AverageExpression(
    seurat_obj,
    features = features_present,
    assays = "integrated",
    slot = "data"
  )$integrated

  return(avg_expr)
}

# --- Calculate for Surface Markers ---
avg_human_surface <- get_avg_expression(human_integrated_annotated, surface_marker_map$human)
avg_rhesus_surface <- get_avg_expression(rhesus_integrated_annotated, surface_marker_map$rhesus)

# --- Calculate for Phospho Markers ---
avg_human_phospho <- get_avg_expression(human_integrated_annotated, phospho_marker_map$feature_name)
avg_rhesus_phospho <- get_avg_expression(rhesus_integrated_annotated, phospho_marker_map$feature_name)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Heatmap Generation Function
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Purpose: A reusable function to create scaled, side-by-side heatmaps with a labeled legend.

create_comparison_heatmap <- function(human_avg_expr, rhesus_avg_expr, marker_map, main_title, filename) {

  # --- 1. Align Data ---
  # Ensure both matrices have the same markers in the same order.
  if ("human" %in% colnames(marker_map)) { # This is the surface marker map
      human_map <- setNames(marker_map$display_name, marker_map$human)
      rhesus_map <- setNames(marker_map$display_name, marker_map$rhesus)
      
      rownames(human_avg_expr) <- human_map[rownames(human_avg_expr)]
      rownames(rhesus_avg_expr) <- rhesus_map[rownames(rhesus_avg_expr)]
      
  } else { # This is the phospho marker map
      rownames(human_avg_expr) <- marker_map$display_name[match(rownames(human_avg_expr), marker_map$feature_name)]
      rownames(rhesus_avg_expr) <- marker_map$display_name[match(rownames(rhesus_avg_expr), marker_map$feature_name)]
  }

  common_markers <- intersect(rownames(human_avg_expr), rownames(rhesus_avg_expr))
  human_aligned <- human_avg_expr[common_markers, ]
  rhesus_aligned <- rhesus_avg_expr[common_markers, ]
  
  # --- 2. Create a Common Color Scale ---
  # Scale data by row (marker) to get z-scores
  human_scaled <- t(scale(t(human_aligned)))
  rhesus_scaled <- t(scale(t(rhesus_aligned)))
  
  global_min <- min(min(human_scaled, na.rm=T), min(rhesus_scaled, na.rm=T))
  global_max <- max(max(human_scaled, na.rm=T), max(rhesus_scaled, na.rm=T))
  color_breaks <- seq(global_min, global_max, length.out = 101)
  
  heatmap_colors <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(n = 7, name = "RdYlBu")))(100)

  # --- 3. Generate pheatmap objects ---
  # We generate them silently to arrange them with grid.arrange
  p_human <- pheatmap(
    human_scaled,
    main = "Human",
    cluster_rows = FALSE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    fontsize_row = 10,
    color = heatmap_colors,
    breaks = color_breaks,
    legend_title = "z-score", # <-- ADDED LEGEND TITLE
    silent = TRUE
  )
  
  p_rhesus <- pheatmap(
    rhesus_scaled,
    main = "Rhesus",
    cluster_rows = FALSE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    fontsize_row = 10,
    color = heatmap_colors,
    breaks = color_breaks,
    legend_title = "z-score", # <-- ADDED LEGEND TITLE
    silent = TRUE
  )
  
  # --- 4. Arrange and Save Plot ---
  tiff(filename, width = 16, height = 10, units = 'in', res = 300)
  
  grid.arrange(
    p_human[[4]], 
    p_rhesus[[4]], 
    ncol = 2,
    top = textGrob(main_title, gp = gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold"))
  )
  
  dev.off()
  
  cat(paste("Heatmap saved to:", filename, "\n"))
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate and Save the Plots to a Defined Path
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Purpose: Call the function to create and save both sets of heatmaps.

# Create the directory if it doesn't exist. 'recursive = TRUE' creates parent directories if needed.
dir.create(output_path, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# --- Generate Surface Marker Heatmap ---
if (!is.null(avg_human_surface) && !is.null(avg_rhesus_surface)) {
  create_comparison_heatmap(
    human_avg_expr = avg_human_surface,
    rhesus_avg_expr = avg_rhesus_surface,
    marker_map = surface_marker_map,
    main_title = "Mean Expression of Surface Markers by Cell Type",
    filename = file.path(output_path, "Species_Difference_Surface_Markers_Comparison.tiff")
  )
}

# --- Generate Phospho Marker Heatmap ---
if (!is.null(avg_human_phospho) && !is.null(avg_rhesus_phospho)) {
  create_comparison_heatmap(
    human_avg_expr = avg_human_phospho,
    rhesus_avg_expr = avg_rhesus_phospho,
    marker_map = phospho_marker_map,
    main_title = "Mean Expression of Phospho-Proteins by Cell Type",
    filename = file.path(output_path, "Species_Difference_Phospho_Markers_Comparison.tiff")
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Donor IDs are stored in "sample" column for the seurat object
human_donors <- unique(human_integrated_annotated$sample)

# Create an empty list to store data frames per donor
human_cluster_counts_list <- list()

# For each donor, compute cluster counts and proportions
for (donor in human_donors) {
  # Subset data for the donor
  donor_cells <- subset(human_integrated_annotated, subset = sample == donor)
  
  # Get total cells for the donor
  total_cells_donor <- ncol(donor_cells)
  
  # Compute cluster counts
  donor_cluster_counts <- table(donor_cells$QBC_annotation_cross_species)
  
  # Convert to data frame
  donor_cluster_counts_df <- as.data.frame(donor_cluster_counts)
  colnames(donor_cluster_counts_df) <- c("Cluster", "Cell_Count")
  
  # Calculate proportions
  donor_cluster_counts_df$Proportion <- donor_cluster_counts_df$Cell_Count / total_cells_donor * 100
  
  # Add donor and species information
  donor_cluster_counts_df$Donor <- donor
  donor_cluster_counts_df$Species <- "Human"
  
  # Add to list
  human_cluster_counts_list[[donor]] <- donor_cluster_counts_df
  
  # Combine data frames from all donors
human_cluster_counts_df <- bind_rows(human_cluster_counts_list)
}
```

```{r}
# Merge donor-level data from both species
combined_cluster_counts_df <- bind_rows(human_cluster_counts_df, rhesus_cluster_counts_df)

# Find common clusters between human and rhesus data
common_clusters <- intersect(human_cluster_stats$Cluster, rhesus_cluster_stats$Cluster)

# Initialize data frame to store test results
stat_test_results <- data.frame(
  Cluster = character(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  adj_p_value = numeric(),
  test = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Make sure we're using dplyr's filter
library(dplyr)

# Perform statistical test for each common cluster
for (cluster in common_clusters) {
  # Subset data for the cluster
  cluster_data <- combined_cluster_counts_df %>% 
    dplyr::filter(.data$Cluster == cluster)
  
  # Get proportions for each species
  human_props <- cluster_data %>% 
    dplyr::filter(.data$Species == "Human") %>% 
    pull(Proportion)
  rhesus_props <- cluster_data %>% 
    dplyr::filter(.data$Species == "Rhesus") %>% 
    pull(Proportion)
  
  # Check sample sizes
  n_human <- length(human_props)
  n_rhesus <- length(rhesus_props)
  
  # Perform Wilcoxon rank-sum test (non-parametric)
  test_result <- wilcox.test(human_props, rhesus_props)
  
  # Store the result
  stat_test_results <- rbind(stat_test_results, data.frame(
    Cluster = cluster,
    p_value = test_result$p.value,
    test = "Wilcoxon rank-sum",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# Add adjusted p-values
stat_test_results$adj_p_value <- p.adjust(stat_test_results$p_value, method = "BH")
```

```{r}
# Perform statistical tests for each comparison
# Function to run Wilcoxon test for a specific cluster between species
run_wilcox_test <- function(data, cluster_name) {
  human_props <- data %>% 
    dplyr::filter(.data$Species == "Human", .data$Cluster == cluster_name) %>% 
    pull(Proportion)
  
  rhesus_props <- data %>% 
    dplyr::filter(.data$Species == "Rhesus", .data$Cluster == cluster_name) %>% 
    pull(Proportion)
  
  test_result <- wilcox.test(human_props, rhesus_props)
  
  return(data.frame(
    Cluster = cluster_name,
    p_value = test_result$p.value,
    test = "Wilcoxon rank-sum",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# Run tests for monocyte populations
monocyte_results <- bind_rows(
  run_wilcox_test(monocyte_comparison, "Classical_monocytes"),
  run_wilcox_test(monocyte_comparison, "Non-classical_monocytes")
)
monocyte_results$adj_p_value <- p.adjust(monocyte_results$p_value, method = "BH")

# Print results
print("Monocyte comparison results:")
print(monocyte_results)
```

```{r}
# Define the function
plot_phospho_marker_across_clusters <- function(seurat_obj, phospho_markers, save_path, species_name = "Human", cluster_names = NULL) {
  
  # Set cluster identities to 'QBC_annotation_cross_species'
  Idents(seurat_obj) <- 'QBC_annotation_cross_species'
  
  # Subset the Seurat object to include only the specified clusters (if provided)
  if (!is.null(cluster_names)) {
    seurat_obj <- subset(seurat_obj, idents = cluster_names)
  }
  
  # Iterate over each phospho marker
  for (marker in phospho_markers) {
    # Create the violin plot
    p <- VlnPlot(
      object = seurat_obj,
      features = marker,
      pt.size = 0
    ) +
      ggtitle(paste(species_name, "-", marker)) +
      ylab("Expression Level") +
      xlab("Cluster") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.25)) +  # Set y-axis limits to [0, 1]
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
      )
    
    # Save the plot
    file_name <- paste0(species_name, "_", gsub("[ /]", "_", marker), "_expression_by_clusters.tiff")
    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(save_path, file_name),
      plot = p,
      width = 12,
      height = 8
    )
  }
}
```

##Trajectory Analysis using Monocle3
# Differential Expression Along Trajectories: Monocle 3 provides tools suitable for protein data to identify proteins whose expression varies along the trajectory.
# Complex Trajectories: If your data exhibit complex branching patterns, Monocle 3 may capture these more effectively.
# Integration with Existing Annotations: Monocle 3 allows for easy integration of existing annotations (e.g., cell types, markers) into the trajectory analysis and visualization.
```{r}
# --- Master Function for Monocle3 Trajectory Analysis ---

run_monocle_trajectory <- function(seurat_obj, species_name, proliferation_sig, save_path, show_graph = TRUE) {
  
  message(paste("--- Starting Monocle3 analysis for", species_name, "---"))
  
  # 1. Create Monocle cell_data_set (CDS) from Seurat object
  message("Step 1: Converting Seurat object to Monocle CDS...")
  expr_data <- GetAssayData(seurat_obj, slot = "data")
  cell_metadata <- seurat_obj@meta.data
  feature_metadata <- data.frame(gene_short_name = rownames(expr_data), row.names = rownames(expr_data))
  
  cds <- new_cell_data_set(
    expression_data = expr_data,
    cell_metadata = cell_metadata,
    gene_metadata = feature_metadata
  )
  
  # 2. Preprocess, reduce dimensions, and cluster
  message("Step 2: Preprocessing and clustering cells...")
  cds <- preprocess_cds(cds, num_dim = 50, norm_method = "none")
  cds <- reduce_dimension(cds, reduction_method = "UMAP", preprocess_method = "PCA")
  cds <- cluster_cells(cds, reduction_method = "UMAP")
  
  # 3. Learn the trajectory graph
  message("Step 3: Learning trajectory graph...")
  cds <- learn_graph(cds)
  
  # 4. Define root cells using the proliferation signature
  message("Step 4: Identifying root cells based on proliferation signature...")
  
  available_markers <- names(proliferation_sig)[names(proliferation_sig) %in% rownames(expr_data)]
  message(paste("Using the following", length(available_markers), "markers for proliferation score:", paste(available_markers, collapse=", ")))
  
  normalized_expr <- t(scale(t(expr_data[available_markers, ])))
  proliferation_score <- colMeans(normalized_expr, na.rm = TRUE)
  cds@colData$proliferation_score <- proliferation_score
  
  score_threshold <- quantile(proliferation_score, 0.95)
  root_cells <- colnames(cds)[proliferation_score >= score_threshold]
  message(paste("Identified", length(root_cells), "root cells."))
  
  # 5. Order cells in pseudotime
  message("Step 5: Ordering cells along the trajectory...")
  cds <- order_cells(cds, root_cells = root_cells)

  # 6. Generate and save all plots as PDFs
  message("Step 6: Generating and saving output plots...")
  
  # Plot 1: Trajectory colored by Cell Type ('QBC_annotation_cross_species')
  pdf(file.path(save_path, paste0(species_name, "_trajectory_by_celltype.pdf")), width = 12, height = 10)
  print(plot_cells(cds, color_cells_by = "QBC_annotation_cross_species", label_cell_groups = TRUE, show_trajectory_graph = show_graph)) # <-- REVISED
  dev.off()
  
  # Plot 2: Trajectory colored by Pseudotime
  pdf(file.path(save_path, paste0(species_name, "_trajectory_by_pseudotime.pdf")), width = 10, height = 8)
  print(plot_cells(cds, color_cells_by = "pseudotime", show_trajectory_graph = show_graph))
  dev.off()
  
  # Plot 3: Trajectory colored by Proliferation Score
  pdf(file.path(save_path, paste0(species_name, "_trajectory_by_proliferation.pdf")), width = 10, height = 8)
  print(plot_cells(cds, color_cells_by = "proliferation_score", show_trajectory_graph = show_graph))
  dev.off()
  
  message(paste("--- Analysis for", species_name, "complete. ---"))
  return(cds)
}
```


```{r}
# --- Final Heatmap Function Using ComplexHeatmap ---
plot_pseudotime_heatmap <- function(cds_obj, top_markers, species_name, save_path) {
  
  # 1. Prepare data
  pseudotime_data <- pseudotime(cds_obj)
  pseudotime_data <- pseudotime_data[is.finite(pseudotime_data)]
  ordered_cells <- names(sort(pseudotime_data))
  
  expr_matrix <- SingleCellExperiment::counts(cds_obj)[top_markers, ordered_cells]
  row_variances <- apply(expr_matrix, 1, var)
  expr_matrix_filtered <- expr_matrix[row_variances > 0, ]
  
  if (nrow(expr_matrix_filtered) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No markers with variance found for", species_name, "- skipping heatmap."))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  scaled_matrix <- t(scale(t(expr_matrix_filtered)))
  
  # 2. Create annotation bars for the top of the heatmap
  cell_annotations <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    Cell_Type = colData(cds_obj)[ordered_cells, "QBC_annotation_cross_species"], # <-- REVISED
    Pseudotime = anno_points(pseudotime_data[ordered_cells])
  )
  
  # 3. Create the Heatmap
  final_heatmap <- Heatmap(
    scaled_matrix,
    name = "Z-score",
    cluster_columns = FALSE,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    show_column_names = FALSE,
    column_title = paste("Protein Expression in", species_name, "(Cells Ordered by Pseudotime)"),
    top_annotation = cell_annotations,
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
      title = "Z-score",
      title_position = "topcenter",
      legend_direction = "horizontal",
      legend_width = unit(5, "cm")
    )
  )
  
  # 4. Save the plot to a PDF
  pdf(file.path(save_path, paste0(species_name, "_Top_Proteins_Heatmap.pdf")), width = 12, height = 8)
  draw(final_heatmap, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
  dev.off()
  
  message(paste("Saved final heatmap for", species_name))
}
```

```{r}
# --- 1. Define the Proliferation Signature ---

proliferation_signature <- c(
  "Ki67-CyTOF" = 1.0, "HLA.DR-CyTOF" = 1.0, "pS6.S235.S236.-CyTOF" = 1.0,
  "p4EBP1.T37.T46.-CyTOF" = 1.0, "pERK1.2.T202.Y204.-CyTOF" = 1.0,
  "HLA.DR-QBC" = 1.0, "CD71-QBC" = 1.0, "CD25-QBC" = 1.0, "CD69-QBC" = 1.0
)

# --- 2. Execute the Trajectory Analysis ---

# Define the save path
trajectory_save_path <- file.path(output_path, "trajectory_analysis_results_no_graph")
dir.create(trajectory_save_path, showWarnings = FALSE)

rhesus_top_proteins <- rhesus_deg_sig %>% arrange(desc(morans_I)) %>% pull(gene_short_name) %>% head(10)

)

  cds_obj = rhesus_cds,
  top_markers = rhesus_top_proteins,
  species_name = "Rhesus",
  save_path = trajectory_save_path
)
```

```{r}
# --- Custom Function to Plot Pseudotime with Cell Type Labels ---

plot_pseudotime_with_labels <- function(cds_obj,
                                        species_name,
                                        save_path,
                                        label_size = 8,
                                        label_alpha = 0.6,
                                        base_font_size = 18,
                                        width = 12,
                                        height = 10) {

  message(paste("--- Generating enhanced UMAP plot for", species_name, "---"))

  # 1. Extract necessary data from the CDS object
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    UMAP_1 = reducedDims(cds_obj)$UMAP[, 1],
    UMAP_2 = reducedDims(cds_obj)$UMAP[, 2],
    pseudotime = pseudotime(cds_obj),
    # UPDATED: Using your new annotation column
    cell_type = colData(cds_obj)$QBC_annotation_cross_species
  )

  # 2. Calculate the center of each cell type cluster
  label_positions <- plot_data %>%
    group_by(cell_type) %>%
    summarize(
      median_UMAP_1 = median(UMAP_1),
      median_UMAP_2 = median(UMAP_2)
    )

  # 3. Create the ggplot object
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = UMAP_1, y = UMAP_2)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = pseudotime), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Pseudotime") +

    # 4. Add translucent labels
    geom_label_repel(
      data = label_positions,
      aes(x = median_UMAP_1, y = median_UMAP_2, label = cell_type),
      size = label_size,
      fill = alpha("white", label_alpha),
      box.padding = unit(0.7, "lines"),
      point.padding = unit(0.4, "lines"),
      segment.color = 'grey50',
      max.overlaps = Inf
    ) +

    # 5. Add titles and theme
    labs(
      title = paste(species_name, "Trajectory"),
      subtitle = "Cells colored by pseudotime with cell type labels"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = base_font_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_font_size * 1.2, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_font_size * 0.9),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_font_size, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = base_font_size * 0.8),
      legend.position = "right"
    )

  # 6. Save the plot to a PDF file
  file_name <- file.path(save_path, paste0(species_name, "_trajectory_pseudotime_with_labels.pdf"))
  pdf(file_name, width = width, height = height)
  print(p)
  dev.off()

  message(paste("Plot saved to:", file_name))
}
```

```{r}
# --- Custom Function to Plot Proliferation Score with Cell Type Labels ---

plot_proliferation_with_labels <- function(cds_obj,
                                           species_name,
                                           save_path,
                                           label_size = 8,
                                           label_alpha = 0.6,
                                           base_font_size = 18,
                                           width = 12,
                                           height = 10) {

  message(paste("--- Generating enhanced UMAP proliferation plot for", species_name, "---"))

  # 1. Extract necessary data from the CDS object
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    UMAP_1 = reducedDims(cds_obj)$UMAP[, 1],
    UMAP_2 = reducedDims(cds_obj)$UMAP[, 2],
    # UPDATED: Use proliferation_score instead of pseudotime
    proliferation_score = colData(cds_obj)$proliferation_score,
    cell_type = colData(cds_obj)$QBC_annotation_cross_species
  )

  # 2. Calculate the center of each cell type cluster
  label_positions <- plot_data %>%
    group_by(cell_type) %>%
    summarize(
      median_UMAP_1 = median(UMAP_1),
      median_UMAP_2 = median(UMAP_2)
    )

  # 3. Create the ggplot object
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = UMAP_1, y = UMAP_2)) +
    # UPDATED: Color points by proliferation_score
    geom_point(aes(color = proliferation_score), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    # UPDATED: Change the legend title
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Proliferation\nScore") +

    # 4. Add translucent labels (no changes here)
    geom_label_repel(
      data = label_positions,
      aes(x = median_UMAP_1, y = median_UMAP_2, label = cell_type),
      size = label_size,
      fill = alpha("white", label_alpha),
      box.padding = unit(0.7, "lines"),
      point.padding = unit(0.4, "lines"),
      segment.color = 'grey50',
      max.overlaps = Inf
    ) +

    # 5. Add titles and theme
    labs(
      title = paste(species_name, "Proliferation Score"), # UPDATED: Title
      subtitle = "Cells colored by proliferation score with cell type labels" # UPDATED: Subtitle
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = base_font_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_font_size * 1.2, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_font_size * 0.9),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_font_size, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = base_font_size * 0.8),
      legend.position = "right"
    )

  # 6. Save the plot to a PDF file
  # UPDATED: New filename
  file_name <- file.path(save_path, paste0(species_name, "_trajectory_proliferation_with_labels.pdf"))
  pdf(file_name, width = width, height = height)
  print(p)
  dev.off()

  message(paste("Plot saved to:", file_name))
}
```

##Trajectory Analysis using Slingshot

```{r}
#Extract the Necessary Data

human_assay_data <- GetAssayData(
  object = human_integrated_annotated,
  slot = "data",
  assay = DefaultAssay(human_integrated_annotated)
)

rhesus_assay_data <- GetAssayData(
  object = rhesus_integrated_annotated,
  slot = "data",
  assay = DefaultAssay(rhesus_integrated_annotated)
)
```

```{r}
# Extract cell metadata
human_cell_metadata <- human_integrated_annotated@meta.data

rhesus_cell_metadata <- rhesus_integrated_annotated@meta.data
```

```{r}
# Extract UMAP embeddings
human_umap_embeddings <- Embeddings(
  object = human_integrated_annotated,
  reduction = "umap"
)

rhesus_umap_embeddings <- Embeddings(
  object = rhesus_integrated_annotated,
  reduction = "umap"
)
```


```{r}
# Create SingleCellExperiment object
human_sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
  assays = list(logcounts = human_assay_data),
  colData = human_cell_metadata,
  reducedDims = list(UMAP = human_umap_embeddings)
)

rhesus_sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
  assays = list(logcounts = rhesus_assay_data),
  colData = rhesus_cell_metadata,
  reducedDims = list(UMAP = rhesus_umap_embeddings)
)

#Assay Naming: In SingleCellExperiment, the assay containing normalized log-transformed counts is often named logcounts
```

```{r}
# Run Slingshot
human_sce <- slingshot(
  human_sce,
  clusterLabels = 'QBC_annotation_cross_species',
  reducedDim = 'UMAP'
)
```

```{r}
rhesus_sce <- slingshot(
  rhesus_sce,
  clusterLabels = 'QBC_annotation_cross_species',
  reducedDim = 'UMAP'
)
```
